title: Reduce GPU memory and workspace: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, arena tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory and transient workspace usage via optional layerwise activation checkpointing, earlier scratch buffer frees, and allocator arena tuning. Config flags exposed: runtime.activate_checkpointing.enabled, runtime.scratch_buffer.scope_release, runtime.allocator.arena_max_chunk. No API break.
description: Motivation: reduce GPU peak memory and transient workspace allocations in the serving runtime to avoid OOMs on 16GB-class GPUs and reduce fragmentation for long-sequence and batchy workloads. Summary: this PR implements optional layerwise activation checkpointing for causal transformer layers (configurable per-model), introduces a scoped scratch buffer lifetime mechanism to free scratch memory immediately after kernel use, and applies conservative arena allocator tuning (smaller max chunk, adjusted growth factor) to reduce fragmentation. The change is gated behind runtime config flags and disabled by default for backcompat. The change set includes microbenchmarks and end-to-end integration tests. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4521) - [x] Core implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests on GPU infra - [x] Microbenchmarks and regression checks - [x] Documentation and runtime flag surface - [x] Patch for hotfix branch if needed (none required) Benchmarks: on internal generation workload (8k input, 512 tokens generation, batch size 4) we observe ~25% lower peak GPU memory across models tested (gpt-medium-family), a ~12% p99 latency improvement due to fewer OOM-driven retries and lower memory thrash, and no regression in throughput for small-sequence workloads. Risk/compatibility: feature is opt-in via runtime.activate_checkpointing.enabled and per-model config. Scratch buffer scope_release is safe to enable cluster-wide after a short monitoring window. Arena tuning is conservative; we validated against long-lived multi-tenant workloads. Testing performed: unit tests, GPU integration tests against 16GB and 40GB nodes, perf canary runs, and a limited rollout on dedicated cluster. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and evaluation prompts.

review_comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Can we make checkpointing per-layer granularity so we avoid extra recompute for small layers? Response: implemented layerwise gating and added per-layer cost heuristics (see checkpointing.cpp lines ~210-260).

Thomas Nguyen (reviewer): allocator changes may affect long-lived fragments under multi-tenant load; did you validate with the mem-stress harness? Response: ran mem-stress for 48h on dedicated cluster; added fragmentation metric and alarm thresholds to Console (added metrics allocator.fragmentation_ratio).
Lina Chen (reviewer): please add opt-out flag at model config level. Response: added runtime.activate_checkpointing.per_model flag and updated model config parser.

QA (comment): observed flaky failure in tests/Integration on older CUDA driver during canary; root cause was timing in scratch buffer free. Fix: introduced small synchronization fence around free and warmed up canary nodes.
